security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown formatting or schema terms, but the skill intentionally runs RunComfy CLI commands and uses RunComfy network services. Placeholder media URLs are false positives for path traversal. The main residual risks are third-party prompt and media submission, local CLI execution, and token storage.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running RunComfy commands, and document the expected command, input file, and output directory.
Warn users that prompts and media URLs are sent to RunComfy services, and advise against sensitive or unapproved media.
Recommend scoped tokens, token rotation, and RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI. Document how users can remove the local token file.
Use example.com placeholder media URLs to avoid path traversal false positives from https://... examples.

content.value_statement: Short-form video prompts often need precise model settings and reference media rules. This skill guides Seedance 2.0 Pro requests through RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Routes explicit Seedance and ByteDance video requests to the Seedance 2.0 Pro RunComfy endpoint.
Shows inputs for prompt, image, video, audio, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and seed.
Provides RunComfy CLI examples for text-only, image reference, and multimodal video generation.
Explains when to use Seedance 2.0 Pro instead of HappyHorse, Wan, Kling, or LTX.
Documents RunComfy exit codes, token handling, outbound endpoints, and generated file size limits.
limitations: Generated clips are limited to 4 to 15 seconds.
The documented endpoint supports 480p or 720p output only.
Reference media must meet file type, duration, size, and count limits.
The skill depends on the local RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account.

use_cases.title: Create dialogue ads
use_cases.description: Generate short lip-synced spokesperson clips with a character image and direct audio guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan cinematic previs
use_cases.description: Turn shot notes into a concise Seedance prompt with camera motion, lighting, and duration choices.

use_cases.title: Localize brand videos
use_cases.description: Use reference images and translated dialogue to keep identity stable across short language variants.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner text video
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple text-only Seedance clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Seedance 2.0 Pro to create a 5 second 9:16 video of [scene]. Include [tone], [camera motion], and [audio direction].

prompt_templates.title: Image reference ad
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a lip-synced ad from one character image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Seedance ad using this character image: [image URL]. The speaker says [line]. Use warm light and a slow push-in.

prompt_templates.title: Multimodal scene match
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Seedance request using [image URL], [video URL], and [audio URL]. Match the person, setting, and voice tone in an 8 second clip.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced model choice
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose Seedance or another RunComfy model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this video goal: [goal]. Decide whether Seedance 2.0 Pro is the right model. Explain the key settings and limits.

output_examples.input: Create a vertical cafe spokesperson clip with one image reference.
output_examples.output: A concise Seedance plan with 9:16 aspect ratio, 8 second duration, image reference use, warm dialogue, and RunComfy invocation guidance.

output_examples.input: Use a scene video and voice reference for a brand teaser.
output_examples.output: A multimodal request outline that keeps the scene, matches the audio mood, and stays within reference media limits.

output_examples.input: Compare Seedance with Wan for a lip-sync project.
output_examples.output: A routing recommendation that favors Seedance for native short-form dialogue and notes Wan when direct audio control matters more.

best_practices: Put stable identity details in image references, not long text descriptions.
Keep camera movement, mood, lighting, and audio direction clear and consistent.
Confirm media URLs, token handling, and output directories before running the CLI.
anti_patterns: Requesting clips longer than 15 seconds on this endpoint.
Mixing conflicting visual styles across reference media and prompt text.
Sending private prompts, faces, voices, or media URLs without user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It helps generate short cinematic videos with Seedance 2.0 Pro through RunComfy.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects the RunComfy CLI and either login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it use reference media?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents image, video, and audio reference inputs with count, duration, and size limits.

faq.question: What clip length is supported?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports whole-second durations from 4 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Users should avoid private prompts, unpublished media, sensitive faces, and voice references without consent.
